messages:
Maya: Quick follow-up idea from yesterday's ingest cost sync: implement an 'edge compact header' that drops verbose envelope fields and emits a minimal span header to reduce egress/storage. Gateway would optionally keep a compressed tombstone for late resolution. Design thoughts?

Jordan: Sounds promising. Two quick concerns: 1) how do we maintain trace->billing attribution when billing key is populated asynchronously? 2) extra CPU on hot gateways.

Priya: For (1) we can do a small async resolver service that accepts (t, svc) and returns bk within 1s TTL. For (2) we should be able to do a zero-copy map + protobuf encode in the hot path to keep CPU low.

Luca: We should also think about privacy/regulatory: that origin tombstone must be encrypted at rest and auto-rotated keys. If stored for lookup, keep TTL short (hours).

Maya: Agree on both. Proposed invariant: compact header must contain tid, svc, and fmt_ver. billing key if present, otherwise resolver token. Tombstone stored in KVS with K=sha256(tid+svc+seq), TTL=6h default. Tombstone is gzip+AES256.

Jordan: How will sampling interact? If we do sampling after compaction, we'll lose payload for sampled traces. So sampling decision must run before compaction, or we should shadow full envelope for sampled set.

Priya: We can have two modes: 'early-sample' mode (sample pre-compact) and 'shadow-copy' mode (write full envelope to internal S3-like store for 100% fidelity while canary runs).

infra-bot: infra-bot: created github.com/redwood/obs/issues/4999 - edge-compact-header-prototype

Luca: Metrics to add: compact.header_rate, compact.tombstone_store_rate, compact.resolver_latency_p95. Alert if resolver_p95 > 200ms or tombstone_store_errors > 0.1% over 5m.

Maya: Proposed rollout: 1) dev environment proof-of-concept 2) 0.1% canary with shadow-writes 3) 1% with tombstone enabled for subset 4) scale to 10% with metrics gating 5) global. Each step must keep shadow writes for 48h.

Jordan: Engineering tasks: gateway encoder impl, tombstone KVS adapter, resolver service + cache, shadow write sink, e2e perf harness, security review.

Priya: I'll do the resolver and cache + unit tests.

Luca: I'll coordinate security KMS integration and threat model.

Maya: I'll draft the short RFC with payload proto and rollout checklist. Quick proto sketch:
```
message CompactSpanHeader {
  string tid = 1; // trace id
  string svc_sh = 2; // service short id
  string bk = 3; // billing key (optional)
  bytes tomb = 4; // optional compressed tombstone reference key
  string v = 5; // format version
}
```

Maya: Can @Jordan and @Luca review by Friday noon?

Jordan: Yes, will review.

Luca: Yep.

Maya: Thanks, will post RFC link when ready.
